prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1336; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: A claim was opened for a side impact at an intersection, and the claimant is reporting a shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant, who described the collision the same way as in the first report, including the other vehicle entering from the right. The claimant also confirmed being a passenger in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: The police report and two independent witnesses support the account of how the collision happened. Scene photos and the other driver's statement match it as well.

Entry 4: The vehicle damage matches the described impact. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing indicates the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 5: Prior records show major damage to the same areas from an earlier accident that was never reported to us, and the claimant is now presenting that damage as new. The claimant has not yet explained the difference.

Entry 6: Medical records document a shoulder injury, but it is not yet clear whether this collision caused it. No earlier injury to the same shoulder is known.

Entry 7: Treatment has grown to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added several weeks after the collision. An independent medical review has been requested.

Entry 8: Next steps are to obtain the complete prior claim history and the treating physician's notes, complete the independent review, and hold any settlement decision until the results are in.
